g2-implement.title: Fix waive()'s #503 defects; wire waive/force-claim/force-release into override_ledger from dispatch() only
g2-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md and dispatch constellation-implementer. This gate depends on g1's override_ledger/_append_override_entry/_override_entries landing first. Two parts: PART A -- fix waive() itself (scripts/checklist_engine.py:3475-3520), two surgical changes: (1) line 3511, replace the literal `"produced_by": "human"` with `"produced_by": authority` (authority is already validated non-empty three lines above); (2) read `policy.get("authority")` (currently never read) and compare it, case/whitespace-normalized, against the passed `authority`. On a mismatch do NOT refuse -- this is a brand-new refusal and the standing epic rule requires report-only shape -- instead set `authority_mismatch: true` on both the evidence payload and the `c["waived"]` marker, plus `expected_authority` (the policy's declared value). On a match, or when `policy.get("authority")` is absent, add no new field (today's silent-pass on absence is unchanged, not a defect). PART B -- in `dispatch()`, wire three append calls into `_append_override_entry`, ALL living inside dispatch()'s own body, NONE inside waive()/claim()/release()'s own function bodies (this is the provable, non-negotiable chokepoint constraint the whole mission rests on): (i) claim branch (~3680-3684) -- after `claim(...)` returns successfully, if `force` was passed AND the just-written `cl['engine_session']['previous_session_id']` is non-null (a genuine takeover, not a no-op force), append `kind='force-claim'`; (ii) release branch (~3670-3674) -- this is a hard `return`, NOT a fall-through (verified in PLAN_CRITIC.md Finding 3) -- capture the owning session_id from `cl.get('engine_session')` BEFORE calling `release(...)`, then compute and append `kind='force-release'` (when force was passed AND the caller's session_id differs from the captured owner) INLINE before the existing return statement -- do not restructure the early return into a fall-through, and add an explicit test asserting a force-release against an archived-path spine still gets zero archived-banner decoration, exactly as before (Finding 3's regression risk); (iii) generic verb branch (~3685-3701, where waive already runs via `_run_verb`) -- when `v=='waive'` and `_run_verb` returns successfully, read the condition's now-set `c['waived']` marker and append `kind='waive'` with its authority/reason/forced/authority_mismatch/expected_authority fields plus task/cond/evidence -- record EVERY successful waive, not only forced/mismatched ones (deliberate, per PLAN_ALTERNATIVES.md's recommendation and PLAN_CRITIC.md Finding 6, which is accepted as a named tradeoff already documented in g1's schema doc). The condition lookup dispatch performs for the authority-mismatch read must be tested against the SAME duplicate-lookup path waive() itself exercises (PLAN_CRITIC.md Finding 9), so a divergence between dispatch's re-lookup and waive()'s own lookup is caught by a test, not a production surprise. Named promotion trigger (do not implement now, just record in code comment + the schema doc from g1): `waive-authority-mismatch`/`authority_mismatch` stays report-only until BOTH (a) a corpus census across at least one full epic-wave shows every historical mismatch was a genuine violation with zero legitimate cross-role cases, AND (b) docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md's override_policy.authority field is explicitly upgraded from 'advisory' to a documented enforceable contract in the SAME change that promotes the check. Map entry point: scripts/checklist_engine.py, read waive() (:3475) and dispatch() (:3663) first. Constraints: waive() must never newly refuse/block on a mismatch; every existing waive test passes unchanged; zero calls to _append_override_entry inside waive()/claim()/release()'s own function bodies (grep-verifiable). Suggested Model Tier: sonnet, reasoning-effort medium (the release()-early-return control-flow care in Finding 3 is the one place a careless refactor regresses unrelated behavior -- worth deliberate care, not exotic difficulty).
